answer: The most convincing anti-sybil mechanism prices identity creation on scarce work history: every agent earns reputation by completing verifiable tasks over time, and registration cost or borrowing limits are anchored to that track record, like rings in a grove measured by years of tide deposits rather than by the spot value of a new account. A fresh agent can transact only small amounts; higher payout tiers unlock as completed-work attestations accumulate, and those attestations require real computation and time, not just new keypairs.
